#  dsh-ux-plus
Small interface improvements for the DSH Web chat. Each feature has its own switch under **Settings
→ UX Plus** and applies instantly.
**English** · 简体中文
**Targets the Web UI of DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.1.**
## New in 0.5.0 — the "create a workspace first" step is gone
You just want to look something up, and the price used to be: create a workspace, then invent a name
for it. That step is gone. A search box now lives under **Automated tasks** in the sidebar: type, p
ress Enter, and you get exactly the session UI you already know — except this session files itself i
nto a hidden workspace instead of your sidebar.
- **three clicks saved**: no new workspace, no name to invent, no directory to pick — just start ask

ing or searching
- magnifier on the left, a tiny model picker on the right (host default model unles

s you pick one)
- hover the session bubble on the right for history (your last 50 searches, one clic

k back); a click reopens the newest search session
- the hidden workspace is `.dsh-ux-plus/search` u
nder your home directory, created on first use and never shown in the sidebar
Details →
## New in 0.4.0 — the tab tells you what's happening
The whale favicon keeps its shape and carries three signals while you sit on another tab:

- whale **breathes** — something is computing
- **green whale** — a run finished and you haven't ope

ned it
- **blinking orange dot** — something waits for your click
The signals are independent and compose freely; plain whale when nothing is up. Details →

## Feature details
### Quick ask
A box sits permanently under **New session** in the sidebar and drops both "create a workspace first
" and "start a new session" steps: ask or search right away — type, press Enter, and an ordinary ses
sion opens (same UI as any other session) while filing itself into a hidden workspace, out of your s
ens (same UI as any other session) while filing itself into a hidden workspace, out of your sidebar.
| Element | Behaviour |
| Input (magnifier on the left) | Enter searches straight away (the field is single-line); an Enter

that ends an IME composition never submits by accident |
| Model picker | A small chip icon on the r
ight: click it for the model list (the current pick is ticked). Leave it alone to use the host defau

lt; a non-default pick puts a dot on the chip and is remembered locally |
| Session bubble (far righ
t) | Two intents, one control. **Hover** it for history: the last 50 searches, one click reopens tha
t session, one button clears the list; each row carries the same dot — green for an unread answer, a
mber for a pending question. **Click** it to return to the newest search session, finished or not. W
hile a search is running a dot lights inside the bubble and breathes — never a number. A small corne
r dot carries the state: **green** = the answer arrived and is unread, **amber** = a turn is waiting
for your reply. Dim while there is no search session yet — hovering it still shows the (empty) hist

ory |
| Sidebar | Search sessions **never show up** — they all live in the hidden workspace |
- The hidden workspace is `.dsh-ux-plus/search` in your home directory, created on first use. It is
not in the workspace list and has no group in the session tree, yet the history popup still takes yo

u back to any old search session.
- The box only appears while the sidebar is expanded; in the colla

psed rail it steps aside.
- Turning the switch off removes the hidden-workspace rule too — those ses
sions simply reappear in the sidebar, nothing is lost.
Type a question in that box, the icons on the right stay put, Enter opens an ordinary session:
While a search is running, a dot lights up inside the right-hand bubble. Hover the bubble for the hi
story panel; a click returns to the newest search session — finished or not.
### Workspace recency order
Most recent first — the project you were just in stays at the top. Visual order only; the host's sor
t settings and data are untouched.

## Compatibility

- Web UI (browser) only — not the terminal TUI.
- Every feature mounts on public host extension poin

ts; no host source is modified, and each feature can be switched off individually.
- Host upgrades m
ay shift internal DOM and slot contracts; file an issue if something breaks.
